item.title: Iran security chief meets Supreme Leader after talks with Mecca pact countries
item.description:
DUBAI, Oct 27 (Reuters) - Iranian Security Council chief Mohsen Rezaei on Tuesday met Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, not seen in public since succeeding his slain father in March, a day after holding talks with representatives of Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan.

State media said Khamenei had stressed the importance of pursuing Iran's interests and maintaining its conditions for ending the war.

item.title: Iranian strait authority says Sinokor vessels will face legal action
item.description:
DUBAI, Oct 27 (Reuters) - Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority, a body set up by Tehran to manage passage requests in the Strait of Hormuz, said on Tuesday all vessels belonging to South Korean shipping company Sinokor would face "legal action" starting on November 1.

Tehran has sought to tighten its grip on the strategic waterway by attacking shipping there since ​US and Israeli ⁠airstrikes on Iran on February 28. It has restricted transit to try to gain leverage over Washington, while disrupting oil flows from Arab Gulf oil producers, especially to their customers in Asia.

item.title: Dutch broadcaster pulls out of Eurovision over Israel 'sensitivities'
item.description:
The Netherlands will not participate in next year's Eurovision Song Contest, its public broadcaster NPO said Tuesday, citing "sensitivities" over Israel's participation.

The Dutch withdrawal is the latest in a series of boycotts from countries unhappy at Israel's inclusion in the annual music festival, given its military campaign in Gaza sparked by the October 7 Hamas attacks.

item.title: Three Arab states back Greece in dispute over Turkey-Libya maritime accord
item.description:
ATHENS, Oct 27 (Reuters) - Egypt, Bahrain and the United Arab Emirates aligned with Greece to denounce a Turkey-Libya maritime accord as a threat to regional security and international legal order in a long-standing dispute over sea borders in the eastern Mediterranean Sea.

Libya's eastern parliamentlast week approved a maritime boundaries deal with Turkey, originally agreed in 2019, drawing swift condemnation from Greece and Cyprus, which say it infringes on their own maritime claims.

item.title: Yemen's Houthis say they launched an attack on Saudi Ras Tanura oil refinery
item.description:
DUBAI, Oct 27 (Reuters) - Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis said on Tuesday they had launched an attack on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura oil refinery, the ⁠biggest in the kingdom, located on the Gulf west of the Strait of Hormuz.

The group's military spokesperson Yahya Saree said in a statement that the ballistic missile attack caused a fire at the site. The Saudi authorities have not confirmed the attack.

The Houthi militia have escalated their attacks on Saudi Arabia since September, opening another volatile front in the wider US-Israeli war on Iran.

item.title: Jordan says it killed more than 20 Islamic State militants in airstrikes on Syria
item.description:
Oct 27 (Reuters) - Jordan said on Tuesday it had killed more than 20 Islamic State militants in airstrikes on southern Syria the previous evening, launched in response to a deadly church attack in Jordan that authorities linked to militants operating across the border.

Syria said the strikes killed seven people, including three children and a woman. Jordan regretted the civilian casualties, Government Communication Minister Mohammed al-Momani said in a post on X.

item.title: Exclusive-Alleged Israeli spy company heavily targeted Starlink users, sources say
item.description:
By Raphael Satter

WASHINGTON, Oct 27 (Reuters) - Experts at a digital defense firm recently found that an Israeli ad tech company was heavily targeting users ofStarlink's satellite internet service in a likely effort to spy on them, according to six people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Two men charged in UK with helping Iran over RAF Fairford incident
item.description:
LONDON, Oct 27 (Reuters) - Two men were charged under the National Security Act on Tuesday over last month's incident at the RAF Fairford military base, with prosecutors accusing a British national of trying to help Iranian intelligence in Britain.

RAF Fairford had been used by US bombers to carry out strikes on Iran, but they were withdrawn on security grounds shortly after five British men were arrested outside the base in southwest England in the early hours of September 27.

item.title: Iraqi court sentences six French men to life in prison for Islamic State membership
item.description:
BAGHDAD, Oct 27 - An Iraqi court on Tuesday sentenced six French nationals to life in prison and a seventh to 15 years after convicting them of membership in Islamic State, a Reuters witness inside the courtroom said.

The men were among 47 French Islamic State suspects transferred from detention facilities in northeast Syria to Iraq last year under a broader relocation arrangement coordinated by US forces and Iraqi authorities.

item.title: China to send envoy to Middle East in near future amid conflict spillover
item.description:
BEIJING, Oct 27 (Reuters) - China is highly concerned about conflicts in the Middle East and surrounding regions and Beijing will send an envoy to the relevant countries in the near future,foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakunsaid at a daily press conference on Tuesday.

Guo called on related parties to resolve differences through dialogue and negotiation and also expressed concerns about the spillover and transmitting of the Middle East conflict to the Horn of Africa and the Red Sea region.

item.title: In Israel, Eisenkot tries quiet appeal to oust Netanyahu
item.description:
Gadi Eisenkot, the man who could unseat Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, almost always dresses in black, speaks halting English and tends to respond in interviews with bullet-point lists, a reflection of the military culture that shaped him.

For some voters in Tuesday's general election, the 66-year-old's lack of charisma may be one of his greatest assets.

item.title: Benjamin Netanyahu: Israel's longest-serving PM fighting for survival
item.description:
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Israel's consummate political survivor, faces the fight of his life in Tuesday's election as he tries to convince voters he is still the only candidate capable of keeping them safe.

The 77-year-old's security-first reputation was all but shattered by Hamas's October 7, 2023 attack, and his main rival -- ex-military chief Gadi Eisenkot -- has channelled public anger over the failure and is running neck and neck with Netanyahu in polls.

item.title: Israel to give verdict on Netanyahu in pivotal election
item.description: Israelis flocked to the polls on Tuesday for the first time since Hamas's October 7, 2023 attack, with a deeply divided electorate delivering their verdict on vete

item.title: The key issues shaping Israel's election
item.description:
When Israel goes to the polls on Tuesday, voters will weigh in on military conscription, the economy and how the state should investigate its failure to prevent Hamas's October 7, 2023 attack.

AFP looks at the key issues that have shaped the campaign.

- Accountability for October 7 -

Many Israelis have demanded an independent state commission of inquiry into the failures that allowed Hamas's October 7, 2023 attack, which resulted in the deaths of more than 1,200 people.

item.title: Macklemore vows to fight until 'last breath' at opening of 'Free Palestine' tour
item.description:
By Padraic Halpin

DUBLIN, Oct 26 (Reuters) - American rapper Macklemore vowed to continue to speak out loudly against Israel's war in Gaza at the opening of his "Free Palestine" concert tour organised after he was dropped as the opening act for Ed Sheeran over pro-Palestinian remarks.

The Grammy-winning rapper received a deafening ovation in Dublin, where fans in the overwhelmingly pro-Palestinian country came draped in Palestinian flags, black, red and green football jerseys and keffiyeh scarves being sold by vendors outside.

item.title: Jordan strikes militant groups in Syria after church attack
item.description:
The Jordanian military said it had struck "terrorist organisations" in neighbouring Syria on Monday in retaliation for a deadly jihadist attack on a church last week, hours after authorities arrested three men they accused of the killings.

It said air force jets had "destroyed several terrorist positions" and killed and wounded "numerous members" of groups linked to the perpetrators of the church attack.

item.title: Explainer-Israel election: What happens after polls close?
item.description:
By Maayan Lubell

JERUSALEM, Oct 27 (Reuters) - Israel holds a parliamentary election on Tuesday, its first since the Hamas attack on October 7, 2023 that shook the country and plunged the Middle East into turmoil.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's hold on power is at stake, with centrist rivals promising to usher in a new era, but it might take time before clear results are known.

WHEN WILL WE KNOW WHO WON?

It is likely this will be known within a few hours of polls closing, but it could take days or even weeks to become clear.

item.title: Fastest turnout for half a century as Israelis pass wartime judgment on Netanyahu
item.description:
By Steven Scheer and Pesha Magid

JERUSALEM, Oct 27 (Reuters) - Israelis surged to the polls at the fastest rate in nearly half a century on Tuesday to pass wartime judgment on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, in what voters described as the most consequential election in the nation's history.

Long lines formed outside polling stations for the first election since the October 7, 2023, Hamas-led attacks, with voters passionately engaged over the trauma of the country's deadliest day and the ensuing wars in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran.

item.title: Jordan strikes southern Syria after linking church attackers to 'terrorist groups'
item.description:
Oct 26 (Reuters) - Jordan said on Monday its air force struck what it described as militant hideouts in southern Syria after determining that the attackers behind last week's deadly church attack were linked to "terrorist groups" operating there.

There was no immediate comment from Syrian authorities and it was not clear if the strikes were carried out after coordination with Damascus.

(Reporting by Jehad Abu ShalbakEditing by Nick Zieminski)

item.title: Syrian women easy target in Sharaa’s drive to consolidate power
item.description: Syria’s interim president is balancing Western demands for inclusion with pressure from Islamist hard-liners as he seeks to consolidate power and shed his jihadi past.
